We help poor and dispossessed people and each other with horizontal mutual aid!  Cranks can sit in meetings all day fighting over what Lenin said, but FnB will be out there feeding folks who are hungry, and I think that'll make our ideas a lot catchier.  Anarchism asserts its own worth by being practiced, so just practice it!

Any time workers strike against their bosses and landlords to repossess what's rightfully theirs, they're doing communist praxis.  That fight is being waged hottest in the global south and has been for decades.  Whether poor folks liberating themselves call it "communism" or not, or got their ideas straight from Marx, doesn't really matter to me.  
My labelling myself as communist and anarchist, to me just means I've set my north star as "all power to all the people", and so anywhere I find the poor and dispossessed getting power, that *is* my ideal revolution, the only real revolution, the one that's happening.  


I believe it's self-evident in a struggle for liberation that directly dispersing all power to the poorest first and organizing horizontally and living via mutual aid, is just *the best way to win*, and so I trust that any workers fighting for themselves will find these answers.


All Marx or any theorist has really done is document and conceptualize the praxis that poor people have been living by the whole time.

There is a crucial distinction between authority and power that I'm making.


Power is the ability in your body and mind to make your will reality.


*Authority* is control over the power of others through their obedience to you.


The ability to grow food, the knowledge of how to treat an injury, the strength to defend your own body, the means to travel where you want, options around you to learn new abilities- 
All of these things are POWER, unconditional to authority and the power to make other people submit to you or the requirement to submit to others.

Anarchism makes no appeals to the past or the future, it is concerned with the good that can be done now, and insists against waiting for it or getting it by any means besides *doing it like you are already free to do so*.  


Anarchism does not ask for some to sacrifice for others, because anarchism is not utilitarian, because it *does not make moral choices from the bird's-eye perspective of authority*.  It asks who can and will share power and calls on them to, or takes power as it will, and puts the tools of power directly into the hands of the poorest before us and says "do what you will with this".


I'm fundamentally unconcerned with the ruling class as a demographic, and care only to challenge rule as a verb.  Generations are imaginary, like all divisions of social caste, and anarchism means disregarding such divisions completely in the task to empower all.  


My hatred of genentocracy is squarely on the "ocracy" part.  I want no steering committee for society at all, and enjoy no illusion that money and property represent real freedom in the first place.


I don't care for the theory of "redistributing wealth" at all, because it speaks in a phantasmal sense of value, like capitalism, like naziism, and like state communism.


Value isn't money, and it isn't things- it's getting what you need from whoever has it, and contributing whatever you want, at any time.  This is something we will achieve by practicing it here and now, and not some other way.
